steps.text: Beat together butter, shortening, and vanilla with an electric mixer in a large bowl until creamy. Blend in confectioners' sugar, 1 cup at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in milk; continue mixing until icing is light and fluffy. Store icing covered until ready to use.

raw_recipe.headline: Buttercream Icing
raw_recipe.description: This egg-free buttercream icing uses just 5 ingredients to achieve fantastic flavor and the perfect consistency for decorating cookies and cupcakes.
raw_recipe.name: Buttercream Icing

recipeInstructions.text: Beat together butter, shortening, and vanilla with an electric mixer in a large bowl until creamy. Blend in confectioners' sugar, 1 cup at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in milk; continue mixing until icing is light and fluffy. Store icing covered until ready to use.

review.reviewBody: I made two batches. One following the exact recipe, and one with all butter. Defenitely use all butter, the icing turns out just as nice and there is no shortening taste.

Great base recipe; I used all butter, no shortening. I used an extra teaspoon of vanilla and about 4-5 tablespoons of milk. I only used 2½ cups of powdered sugar and found it to be more than enough; I can't imagine the coma I'd be in if I had used 4! I used this icing on the One Bowl Chocolate Cake III (pictured) and I had some left over. The key is clearly to beat at medium to high speed for several minutes to ensure maximum peak. I do recommend this recipe provided you make some minor tweaks... I definitely suggest tasting as you go to ensure that you don't accidentally use too much sugar and have no way to remove the excess. Remember, the best recipes on earth still go through trial and error. =)

I made the buttercream frosting recipe, but used a full cup of butter and used no shortening. I used the paddle attachment on the mixer and beat the butter and added the vanilla extract and also added the seeds of an entire vanilla bean - scraped. I sifted all four cups of confectioners sugar into the bowl - whew! It seemed like it would be too much, but my family and friends went absolutely crazy for the frosting. It pipes easily and smoothly and looks beautiful with an open star tip. It's a recipe that can be easily modified for different flavors - it's my new favorite frosting!

Excellent recipe. I used all butter as others did as I do not like the taste of shortening(Crisco) I also had heavy cream in the fridge I wanted to use up so I used it in place of milk. I used more cream than the recipe called for adding a little at a time until it was the thickness I liked. Don't be afraid to add a tsp at a time until you get the right texture, It does not turn soft quickly. I have been baking since I was 9 and am 63 now. This is my new go to recipe for vanilla frosting. I will add cocoa and see how that works for chocolate frosting. Also I want to say that it is not good for spreading so I just piped it between layers and made pretty flours all over the cake. Ran a little short of frosting so I left the sides nakedish!

Tastes Great
 I normally make a cream cheese icing for the cakes that I bake, But a friend told me that he hates that type of icing and asked me to become a cake so I tried out this recipe. I could tell right away that there was too much sugar in the recipe. By the time I added the 3rd cup the mixture was way too hard. Even when I used the electric mixer it was still too hard. I tasted the mixture after I combine all the ingredients and it was very very tasty. But to get the consistency I needed I added to a table spoons of light cream and 2 tablespoons of coconut rum, since I was making this icing for a coconut rum cake. The icing taste absolutely wonderful. Thank you for posting.

I have made buttercream in the past using only butter and I thought it was to thick and heavy. I came across this recipe and I practically doubled it: 1 cup of butter (2 sticks) and 1 cup of butter flavored shortening (1 stick) and about 5-6 cups of powdered sugar (taste test as you go along so that it’s to your preference of sweetness.) I wanted to make strawberry buttercream so I kept this as a base and added 1/3 cup of sweetened frozen strawberries (with the juice) at the end and it tasted amazing!! This came out beautifully for Valentines Day cupcakes.
Loved it. I followed the suggestions and reduced the sugar. For 12 cupcakes, used 1/2 cup butter, 1-1/4 cup sifted powdered sugar, 1tsp vanilla, and 3T milk. Then whipped it on high for 30 minutes.

This is a good recipe but I made some changes. I used all butter as I don't care for the taste of shortening in the frosting. I also added two teaspoons of vanilla instead of one. I like a frosting less sweet so I used less confectioners sugar. I also added two tablespoons of milk to make it easy to spread.
I used one cup butter instead of the shortening & heavy cream instead of milk. I absolutely love this recipe. I will use this one again!
For those that don't have shortening, or don't have time to run out to the store, I made this with straight butter and it worked great!
Half the confectioners sugar to frost 9x13 cake. Add all butter and just omit shortening.

I use this recipe a lot because I bake a lot! When I make frosting I experiment a lot so you're going to think this is really strange, but I use unsweetened Kool-Aid to make different flavors. The first time I did this I used orange and it was amazing. Be careful not to use too much because it is concentrated, I sprinkle a little at a time. Don't be afraid to be creative most of the time it pays off for me. Enjoy

I followed the recipe exactly and it doesn’t taste good to me. I also had my 9 year old try it and he hated it as well. It spreads easy though that was the only good thing. I’ll keep looking for another recipe.
Perfect creaminess for piping onto cupcakes. I’ll make this one again.
I fowled everything but 1 cup less sugar and Xtra tsp vanilla. Shelf stable and taste good. Always have hard time with frosting. This is perfect for me. Thank you. 😆
Great! Easy to make , fast recipe tastes like it professional

This frosting was too thick. I added another 1/2 cup butter. When I compared it to my 25 year old buttercream frosting recipe (on a tattered old recipe card) I realized that I always used ONE cup of shortening and ONE cup of butter.

I am a newbie to baking but have done a lot of research and tried several different recipes. I do not like the sweetness of frosting /icing but this was PERFECT. I literally could eat on spoon and I normally scrape icing off of cakes.
